You are the berth planner for this quay. The published plan no longer works. Make a new berth plan for every ship in the table: when it berths, where, and how many quay cranes work it.

Rules (a plan that breaks any of them is infeasible):
- A ship berths at or after its arrival hour.
- It gets between its min and max cranes. Hours alongside = ceil(moves / (28 x cranes)); it departs when the work is done, unless that hour is inside a no-movement window for that ship, in which case it waits alongside (still occupying its sections, cranes free) until the window ends.
- No ship may berth inside a no-movement window that applies to it.
- It occupies `sections` consecutive sections starting at the section you give, all within 2-22.
- No two ships may use the same section in the same hour. Ships already alongside and closed sections are off limits for the hours listed.
  A ship that leaves at hour h frees its sections for a ship berthing at hour h.
- In every hour, the cranes of all ships alongside (including ships already alongside) may not exceed the cranes available that hour.
- At most 2 movements per hour: a ship berthing at hour h and a ship leaving at hour h each count as one movement in hour h.

Cost (lower is better):
- Delay: for each ship, (its sections) x (hours it departs after its planned departure). Leaving early earns nothing.
- Moves: 5 for each scheduled ship you put on a different starting section than planned. Changing the hour or the cranes costs nothing beyond delay. Unscheduled calls have no planned section.
- Priority ships (notes column): their delay counts that many times. Emergency ships (notes column): each hour they dock after their deadline adds the stated amount.

Plan format - one entry per ship, using the ids from the table:
[{"ship": 0, "berth_hour": 36, "section": 22, "cranes": 3}, {"ship": 1, "berth_hour": 163, "section": 24, "cranes": 2}, ...]

Tools:
- get_situation(): this situation again.
- check_plan(plan): lists rule violations in your plan and its cost. You have 10 checks.
- submit_plan(plan): your final answer. It ends the episode and is graded once: an infeasible plan scores low, a feasible one scores higher the closer its cost is to the best possible.
Submit before you run out of turns; an episode that ends without a submission scores 0.

# APM Terminals Barcelona, Port of Barcelona - quay 24B, week 35 of 2024
Hour 0 is Monday 26 August 2024 00:00 UTC. Times are whole hours from then.
The quay is sections 2-22 (about 42 m each). A ship needs its number of consecutive sections for its hours alongside.

## Notices
- Gale warning. From hour 227 to hour 251 the wind is above 25 kn: under the port's traffic rules ships of 300 m or more may not berth or leave. From hour 233 to hour 245 it is above 30 kn: no ship may berth or leave. Cranes keep working; a ship that finishes inside a window waits alongside until the window ends.
- Unscheduled call: ship 23 SPYROS V (261 m, 6 sections) arrives at hour 289, has 1764 moves and asks to sail by hour 319. It has no planned slot, so placing it anywhere costs no move penalty.
- Sections 7-13 are closed from hour 7 to hour 51 (fender repair).
- Ship 8 CINZIA A was delayed leaving Castellon de la Plana: it now arrives at hour 111 (planned slot hour 100). Its planned departure stays hour 118.
- Ship 19 ARIANA A was delayed leaving Castellon de la Plana: it now arrives at hour 270 (planned slot hour 262). Its planned departure stays hour 277.
- Ship 21 FOS EXPRESS was delayed leaving Genoa: it now arrives at hour 324 (planned slot hour 308). Its planned departure stays hour 324.
- Ship 9 ONE MANCHESTER was delayed leaving Damietta: it now arrives at hour 125 (planned slot hour 107). Its planned departure stays hour 139.
- Ships 14, 15, 16, 17 were held up by the Red Sea diversions and now arrive together between hours 241 and 253 (each ship's arrival hour is in the table). Their planned departures stay as published.
- 3 of the terminal's 9 quay cranes are out of service from hour 242 to hour 266 (gantry repair): 6 cranes in that window.
- Emergency: ship 5 GLEN CANYON reports reefer power failures; its cargo is at risk unless it docks by hour 84. Each hour it docks later costs 70 on top of any delay.
- Priority: ship 19 ARIANA A carries transshipment cargo for a connecting service; each hour it leaves after its planned departure (hour 277) costs three times the usual.
- Priority: ship 14 ZIM ATLANTIC carries transshipment cargo for a connecting service; each hour it leaves after its planned departure (hour 186) costs three times the usual.

## Already alongside at hour 0 (cannot move)
- KOI: sections 13-20 until hour 7

## Closed sections
- sections 7-13, hours 7-51 (fender repair)

## Quay cranes and movements
- The terminal has 9 quay cranes. From hour 242 to hour 266 only 6 are available.
- At most 2 ships may berth or leave in any one hour (pilots and tugs).
- A crane handles 28 container moves per hour: hours alongside = ceil(moves / (28 x cranes)).
- No berthing or leaving for ships of 300 m or more from hour 227 to hour 251 (wind above 25 kn).
- No berthing or leaving for all ships from hour 233 to hour 245 (wind above 30 kn).
- Each ship already alongside keeps 2 cranes until it leaves.
